imc-brief-xfinity-home-wifi.md.title: Mental Tab Count
imc-brief-xfinity-home-wifi.md.text: The adult in the house is often tracking more than their own screen: whose homework is next, who is working, who is winding down. The creative territory is the quiet mental juggling that makes home internet feel real before anyone talks about it.
imc-brief-xfinity-home-wifi.md.rationale: This makes the objective concrete by locating Xfinity home internet inside the audience’s daily coordination, not in abstract tech language. It gives email and web a relatable human entry point before the product role appears.
imc-brief-xfinity-home-wifi.md.campaignGrounding: Adults coordinating work, homework and entertainment in a shared household.
imc-brief-xfinity-home-wifi.md.hypothesisToValidate: This works if the audience recognizes household coordination as an everyday responsibility rather than a rare conflict.

imc-brief-xfinity-home-wifi.md.excerpt: Adults coordinating work, homework and entertainment in a shared household.
imc-brief-xfinity-home-wifi.md.hypothesis: This works if the audience recognizes household coordination as an everyday responsibility rather than a rare conflict.

imc-brief-xfinity-home-wifi.md.title: The Shared Queue
imc-brief-xfinity-home-wifi.md.text: A household can feel like a living queue, with work, homework and entertainment taking turns without anyone formally announcing it. The territory is the gentle comedy of people making room for each other while every activity has its place in the home.
imc-brief-xfinity-home-wifi.md.rationale: The brief asks for warmth and inclusion, so shared-household humor can make the situation recognizable without blaming any one person. It also keeps the focus on the household’s own activities rather than on product claims.
imc-brief-xfinity-home-wifi.md.hypothesisToValidate: This works if busy households see their daily handoffs as lightly funny and familiar, not as a source of shame or failure.
imc-brief-xfinity-home-wifi.md.idea: A household can feel like a living queue, with work, homework and entertainment taking turns without anyone formally announcing it. The territory is the gentle comedy of people making room for each other while every activity has its place in the home.
imc-brief-xfinity-home-wifi.md.hypothesis: This works if busy households see their daily handoffs as lightly funny and familiar, not as a source of shame or failure.

imc-brief-xfinity-home-wifi.md.title: No Router Hero
imc-brief-xfinity-home-wifi.md.text: Internet advertising often wants to make the technology the main character. This campaign can break that habit by letting the household’s ordinary activities lead, with the product role arriving second and staying in proportion.
imc-brief-xfinity-home-wifi.md.rationale: This directly supports the message hierarchy and avoids unsupported claims about speed, performance or superiority. It gives the campaign a distinct feel: useful, human and modest.
imc-brief-xfinity-home-wifi.md.campaignGrounding: Focus on the household's own activities, not technical boasting.
imc-brief-xfinity-home-wifi.md.hypothesisToValidate: This works if the audience is more open to internet messaging when it reflects their life instead of asking them to admire the technology.
imc-brief-xfinity-home-wifi.md.idea: Internet advertising often wants to make the technology the main character. This campaign can break that habit by letting the household’s ordinary activities lead, with the product role arriving second and staying in proportion.
imc-brief-xfinity-home-wifi.md.excerpt: Focus on the household's own activities, not technical boasting.
imc-brief-xfinity-home-wifi.md.hypothesis: This works if the audience is more open to internet messaging when it reflects their life instead of asking them to admire the technology.

imc-brief-xfinity-home-wifi.md.title: Devices Meet Days
imc-brief-xfinity-home-wifi.md.text: Make the approved product role visible through simple pairings: a device and the online activity someone in the household is trying to do. The Spark is not performance drama, but the everyday fact that home internet sits between devices and the things people came online to do.
imc-brief-xfinity-home-wifi.md.rationale: This keeps the RTB intact while making it easier to understand in human terms. It also gives the creative a disciplined way to show product relevance without inventing features or proof points.
imc-brief-xfinity-home-wifi.md.campaignGrounding: Home internet can connect household devices to online activities.
imc-brief-xfinity-home-wifi.md.hypothesisToValidate: This works if people understand home internet less as a technical object and more as the link between household devices and daily activities.

The Spark is not performance drama, but the everyday fact that home internet sits between devices and the things people came online to do.
imc-brief-xfinity-home-wifi.md.excerpt: Home internet can connect household devices to online activities.
imc-brief-xfinity-home-wifi.md.hypothesis: This works if people understand home internet less as a technical object and more as the link between household devices and daily activities.

imc-brief-xfinity-home-wifi.md.title: The Overlap Hour
imc-brief-xfinity-home-wifi.md.text: There is a daily stretch when work, homework and entertainment all seem to arrive at once. The territory is that visible overlap, when the household’s need for home internet becomes easiest to understand because everyone is trying to move into their next activity.
imc-brief-xfinity-home-wifi.md.rationale: A specific moment helps email and web feel immediate instead of general. It also follows the brief’s hierarchy by starting with the pressure of the household handoff before naming the product role.
imc-brief-xfinity-home-wifi.md.campaignGrounding: Human situation first; supplied product role second.
imc-brief-xfinity-home-wifi.md.hypothesisToValidate: This works if the audience has a recognizable time of day when multiple online activities compete for attention in the same home.
imc-brief-xfinity-home-wifi.md.idea: There is a daily stretch when work, homework and entertainment all seem to arrive at once. The territory is that visible overlap, when the household’s need for home internet becomes easiest to understand because everyone is trying to move into their next activity.
imc-brief-xfinity-home-wifi.md.excerpt: Human situation first; supplied product role second.
imc-brief-xfinity-home-wifi.md.hypothesis: This works if the audience has a recognizable time of day when multiple online activities compete for attention in the same home.

imc-brief-xfinity-home-wifi.md.title: Backstage Cues
imc-brief-xfinity-home-wifi.md.text: Treat the household like a tiny backstage crew: cues, props, entrances and exits, all happening so the next activity can begin. Xfinity’s role stays offstage and practical, helping connect the devices to the online activities as the scene changes.
imc-brief-xfinity-home-wifi.md.rationale: The theater analogy is outside the category but fits the brief’s handoff idea and human-first rule. It creates a fresh visual system for email and web without turning the product into a boastful hero.
imc-brief-xfinity-home-wifi.md.campaignGrounding: Human situation first; supplied product role second.
imc-brief-xfinity-home-wifi.md.hypothesisToValidate: This works if the audience enjoys seeing ordinary household coordination reframed as choreography rather than chaos.

imc-brief-xfinity-home-wifi.md.excerpt: Human situation first; supplied product role second.
imc-brief-xfinity-home-wifi.md.hypothesis: This works if the audience enjoys seeing ordinary household coordination reframed as choreography rather than chaos.

imc-brief-xfinity-mobile-v2.md.title: Plan Brain Drain
imc-brief-xfinity-mobile-v2.md.text: The phone already carries the day; the plan behind it can feel like one more chore hiding inside a busy life. This territory turns mobile shopping into a small but familiar tax on attention.
imc-brief-xfinity-mobile-v2.md.rationale: The objective is to make Xfinity Mobile easier to think about for current Xfinity Internet customers. Naming the mental clutter gives the campaign a relatable enemy without making unverified product claims.
imc-brief-xfinity-mobile-v2.md.campaignGrounding: without having to spend unnecessary time thinking about their phone plans.
imc-brief-xfinity-mobile-v2.md.hypothesisToValidate: This works if the audience feels plan decisions are disproportionately annoying compared with the role phones play in daily life.
imc-brief-xfinity-mobile-v2.md.idea: The phone already carries the day; the plan behind it can feel like one more chore hiding inside a busy life. This territory turns mobile shopping into a small but familiar tax on attention.
imc-brief-xfinity-mobile-v2.md.excerpt: without having to spend unnecessary time thinking about their phone plans.
imc-brief-xfinity-mobile-v2.md.hypothesis: This works if the audience feels plan decisions are disproportionately annoying compared with the role phones play in daily life.

imc-brief-xfinity-mobile-v2.md.title: Household Switchboard
imc-brief-xfinity-mobile-v2.md.text: Phones are where modern households coordinate the tiny stuff: ETAs, dinner votes, kid updates, memes, photos, and last-minute changes. The humor comes from how much life passes through these threads while nobody wants the phone plan to become the main conversation.
imc-brief-xfinity-mobile-v2.md.rationale: This gives the campaign a social canvas for paid social and video: recognizable exchanges rather than abstract service language. It connects mobile choice to the way people already keep their circles moving.
imc-brief-xfinity-mobile-v2.md.campaignGrounding: endless messages, photos, memes, and everyday conversations.
imc-brief-xfinity-mobile-v2.md.hypothesisToValidate: This works if current Xfinity Internet customers see their phone as part of a shared daily rhythm, not just an individual device.
imc-brief-xfinity-mobile-v2.md.idea: Phones are where modern households coordinate the tiny stuff: ETAs, dinner votes, kid updates, memes, photos, and last-minute changes. The humor comes from how much life passes through these threads while nobody wants the phone plan to become the main conversation.
imc-brief-xfinity-mobile-v2.md.excerpt: endless messages, photos, memes, and everyday conversations.
imc-brief-xfinity-mobile-v2.md.hypothesis: This works if current Xfinity Internet customers see their phone as part of a shared daily rhythm, not just an individual device.

imc-brief-xfinity-mobile-v2.md.title: Beyond Bar Wars
imc-brief-xfinity-mobile-v2.md.text: Mobile advertising often gravitates toward deal math, map claims, speed language, and superiority contests. This campaign can feel different by staying with the customer’s lived phone chaos instead of turning the message into a technical courtroom.
imc-brief-xfinity-mobile-v2.md.rationale: The brief’s restrictions push creativity away from common category shortcuts. That can become an advantage by making the work more human, playful, and easier to believe.
imc-brief-xfinity-mobile-v2.md.campaignGrounding: No unsupported claims about savings, pricing, coverage, speed, or network superiority.
imc-brief-xfinity-mobile-v2.md.hypothesisToValidate: This works if the audience is tired of mobile messages that feel like competing fine print rather than help with a real decision.
imc-brief-xfinity-mobile-v2.md.idea: Mobile advertising often gravitates toward deal math, map claims, speed language, and superiority contests. This campaign can feel different by staying with the customer’s lived phone chaos instead of turning the message into a technical courtroom.
imc-brief-xfinity-mobile-v2.md.excerpt: No unsupported claims about savings, pricing, coverage, speed, or network superiority.
imc-brief-xfinity-mobile-v2.md.hypothesis: This works if the audience is tired of mobile messages that feel like competing fine print rather than help with a real decision.

imc-brief-xfinity-mobile-v2.md.title: Everyday Choice Drawer
imc-brief-xfinity-mobile-v2.md.text: Frame Xfinity Mobile as a set of useful everyday choices sitting close to the life people already have with their phones. The product truth is not a grand reinvention of mobile, but a practical fit for ordinary connection needs.
imc-brief-xfinity-mobile-v2.md.rationale: This keeps the RTB vivid while staying within the verified language in the brief. It gives creative a concrete way to show the product without adding claims about price, speed, coverage, or savings.
imc-brief-xfinity-mobile-v2.md.campaignGrounding: with plan and device options designed to support everyday mobile connectivity needs.
imc-brief-xfinity-mobile-v2.md.hypothesisToValidate: This works if the audience wants mobile choices that feel understandable and relevant to normal routines, not overly engineered.
imc-brief-xfinity-mobile-v2.md.idea: Frame Xfinity Mobile as a set of useful everyday choices sitting close to the life people already have with their phones. The product truth is not a grand reinvention of mobile, but a practical fit for ordinary connection needs.
imc-brief-xfinity-mobile-v2.md.excerpt: with plan and device options designed to support everyday mobile connectivity needs.
imc-brief-xfinity-mobile-v2.md.hypothesis: This works if the audience wants mobile choices that feel understandable and relevant to normal routines, not overly engineered.

imc-brief-xfinity-mobile-v2.md.title: Comparison Tab Spiral
imc-brief-xfinity-mobile-v2.md.text: The need peaks when someone finally sits down to compare mobile plans and the tabs, terms, and choices start multiplying. The campaign can live in that recognizable moment when a simple decision begins to feel strangely overgrown.
imc-brief-xfinity-mobile-v2.md.rationale: This moment links directly to the campaign goal of simplifying how people think about mobile choices. It can create strong short-form situations for social, display, email, and site journeys.
imc-brief-xfinity-mobile-v2.md.campaignGrounding: Consumers may find comparing mobile plans confusing.
imc-brief-xfinity-mobile-v2.md.hypothesisToValidate: This works if plan comparison is a real friction point for current Xfinity Internet customers who are open to switching or exploring mobile choices.

imc-brief-xfinity-mobile-v2.md.hypothesis: This works if plan comparison is a real friction point for current Xfinity Internet customers who are open to switching or exploring mobile choices.

imc-brief-xfinity-mobile-v2.md.title: Pocket Stage Manager
imc-brief-xfinity-mobile-v2.md.text: Borrow from theater: the phone is the stage manager calling cues for work, maps, music, photos, errands, and people, while the audience only sees life happening out front. The tension is that the backstage crew is already busy enough without the mobile choice becoming another production.
imc-brief-xfinity-mobile-v2.md.rationale: The theater analogy gives the campaign a fresh way to dramatize the phone’s many roles without making the device itself the hero. It points back to the brief’s everyday-life focus while opening playful visual and narrative possibilities.
imc-brief-xfinity-mobile-v2.md.campaignGrounding: Your phone is your calendar, camera, navigator, entertainment center, and connection to people.
imc-brief-xfinity-mobile-v2.md.hypothesisToValidate: This works if the audience relates to their phone as the unseen organizer of the day, even if they rarely think about the service behind it.

improvedSpark2.title: Are You Done?
improvedSpark2.text: Every shared household has a soft choreography of “Are you done?” and “I’m almost finished,” as work gives way to homework and entertainment waits its turn. The comedy comes from how politely unofficial the system is: everyone knows there’s a line, but no one quite owns it.
improvedSpark2.rationale: This makes the shared behavior more concrete than a general household queue, giving creative teams a repeatable social pattern to dramatize in email or web. It keeps the human situation first and lets Xfinity’s role stay grounded in everyday household activities.
improvedSpark2.campaignGrounding: Adults coordinating work, homework and entertainment in a shared household.
improvedSpark2.hypothesisToValidate: This works if households recognize their daily internet use as a series of small, cooperative handoffs rather than a formal schedule.

improvedSpark2.hypothesis: This works if households recognize their daily internet use as a series of small, cooperative handoffs rather than a formal schedule.

replacedSpark4.title: Household Grammar
replacedSpark4.text: Make the product role vivid as the household’s grammar, not its hero: the small structure that lets a shared home move from “someone has a device” to “someone is doing work, homework or entertainment online.” The tension is that the most useful role in the sentence is not always the loudest word.
replacedSpark4.rationale: This keeps the campaign rooted in everyday household activity while giving the approved product role a fresher visual and verbal frame. It also avoids performance claims by making Xfinity’s role practical and secondary.
replacedSpark4.campaignGrounding: Focus on the household's own activities, not technical boasting.
replacedSpark4.hypothesisToValidate: This works if the audience responds to seeing home internet framed as an ordinary enabler of household action rather than as technology to admire.
